title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. 𝔖^{+∧} is the profinite completion of SL(2,Z). Π^∧ = 𝔖^{+∧}[2] is the closure of the principal congruence subgroup Γ(2). Its quotient by the centre ±1 is π^∧_{0,3}, the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}. Likewise 𝔖^∧_{0,3} ≅ 𝔖^{+∧}/±1 is the completed PSL(2,Z), which acts on π^∧_{0,3} with quotient S_3 (the permutations of the three cusps). M^∼_{0,3}, defined around p.390, is Grothendieck's group of 'admissible' automorphisms: automorphisms of 𝔖^∧_{0,3} preserving π^∧_{0,3} and sending each inertia generator ε_0 to a conjugate of ε_0^μ. Here μ ∈ Ẑ* is the multiplicator, i.e. the cyclotomic character in GT-type language. N^∼_{1,1} is the analogous group attached to M_{1,1}.

Proposition (begun on the previous page). The map M^∼_{0,3} → Aut(𝔖^{+∧}) (lifting through the central extension by ±1, construction 'B)') is injective. Its image consists of the u that (a) stabilize Π^∧, and (b) send ε_0 to a 𝔖^{+∧}-conjugate of ε_0^μ for some μ ∈ Ẑ*.

Necessity. Condition (a) holds because u_0 stabilizes π^∧_{0,3}, so its lift stabilizes the inverse image Π^∧. For (b), compose with an element permuting the cusps to reduce to u_0 ∈ M^∼_{0,3}[0], the stabilizer of cusp 0 up to conjugacy. There, by the construction of N^∼_{1,1} from M^∼_{0,3} (III, p.665), one has u_0(ε_0) = ε_0^μ.

Sufficiency. Given u satisfying (a) and (b), let ũ be the induced automorphism of 𝔖^{+∧}/±1 = 𝔖^∧_{0,3}. Then ũ preserves π^∧_{0,3} and sends ε_0 to a conjugate of ε_0^μ, so ũ ∈ M^∼_{0,3} by definition. Let u' be the canonical lift of ũ. Then Θ = u^{-1}u':
- induces the identity modulo ±1, so Θ(x) = x·χ(x) for a character χ: 𝔖^{+∧} → ±1 (abelianization Z/12);
- sends ε_0 to a conjugate of itself.
Since ε_0 and −ε_0 are not conjugate, even in the profinite completion (remark on the previous page), χ(ε_0) = 1, hence Θ = 1 and u = u'.

Grothendieck then starts the next step. He writes the central extension 1 → ±1 → Π^∧ → π^∧_{0,3} → 1. On the next page he splits it via l_i ↦ λ_i = −l_i, using l_∞l_1l_0 = −1. This yields the index-2 subgroup Π_0 ≅ free group F_2 inside Γ(2) (Γ(2) = ±1 × Π_0), and he shows it is normalized by the whole modular group and its admissible automorphisms.

Purpose. To identify the GT-like group M^∼_{0,3} with a group of automorphisms of the completed SL(2,Z), relating the genus-0 (three-point) and genus-1 (M_{1,1}) towers.
errors: The 'Θ = 1' step needs χ(ε_0) = 1 to force χ trivial. This works because the abelianization of SL(2,Z)^ is Z/12, generated by the image of ε_0 (a parabolic generator), so any character to ±1 is determined by its value on ε_0. Grothendieck only says 'on a vu que cela implique Θ = 1'. It is fine, but relies on the earlier remark.
Mild notational inconsistency: (14) is written u_0(ξ_0) = ε_0^μ (or ξ_0^μ), whereas (13) uses ε_0; ξ_0 and ε_0 appear to denote the same element.
u_0 lives on 𝔖_{0,3} while (14) should refer to its lift to 𝔖^{+∧}. This is implicit.

ideas.what: Characterization of the image of the admissible-automorphism group M~_{0,3} (GT-like, with cyclotomic multiplicator) inside Aut of the profinite completion of SL(2,Z): stabilize Γ(2)^ and send the parabolic ε_0 to a conjugate of ε_0^μ
ideas.modern_name: Action of (a variant of) GT-hat / inertia-preserving automorphisms on SL(2,Z)^ and B_3^; comparison M_{0,4} vs M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps (1997, GT and automorphisms of braid groups); H. Nakamura and collaborators on Out of profinite PSL2/B_3
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only alludes to GT acting on the modular tower; unsure beyond that

ideas.what: Lifting automorphisms through the central extension ±1 → SL2^ → PSL2^, with uniqueness because ε_0 and −ε_0 are not conjugate
ideas.modern_name: Lifting automorphisms through central extensions / characters of SL2(Z)^ab = Z/12

ideas.what: Splitting Γ(2) = ±1 × Π_0 with λ_i = −l_i and l_∞l_1l_0 = −1, and normality of Π_0 in the modular group

missed.claim: An explicit, carefully proved characterization of Grothendieck's M~_{0,3} as a subgroup of Aut(SL(2,Z)^): stabilize the level-2 congruence closure and send ε_0 to a conjugate of a power ε_0^μ. It is essentially known in the later GT literature, but here it is in Grothendieck's own formulation, before 1984 and before Drinfeld/Ihara's GT.
missed.quote: son image est formée des automorphismes u de Ŝ^+ qui satisfont ... a) u stabilise Π^∧ ... b) u transforme L_0 en un sous-groupe ... conjugué
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the GT-action on the completed modular group and the genus-0/genus-1 comparison (cf. Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura). It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct and careful proof of an essentially known statement (the GT-type group acting faithfully on SL(2,Z)^, with image characterized by inertia conditions). It is interesting as unpublished pre-GT Grothendieck material, but the mathematics has since been developed by Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura and others.
transcription_corrections: (14) appears as 'u_0(ξ_0) = ε_0^μ' or with ξ_0 on both sides. Either way ξ_0 ≡ ε_0 in context.
'fixe à conjugaison près un élément' likely refers to fixing the cusp/inertia subgroup (L_0) up to conjugacy.
Line 'Soit u' l'automorphisme ... induit par ũ (via B))' and 'Θ = u^{-1}u'' are correctly read; '2°) transforme L_0^𝔖 en un sous-groupe conjugué' rather than 'ξ_0 en un de ses conjugués'.
Sequence (15) should end with → 1 (Grothendieck writes 0). 𝔖^{+∧}[2] is written under Π^∧ as its identification.
